rules.name: Em dash
rules.message: The em dash reads as AI to many readers.
rules.why: Em dashes are a normal punctuation mark, but AI models use them so often that many readers now treat them as a sign of machine writing.
rules.fix: Use a comma, a colon or parentheses, or split the sentence in two.

flag: The plan worked — mostly.

rules.name: "Delve"
rules.why: AI models use "delve" far more often than people do, so readers now link it to machine writing.

flag: Let's delve into the numbers.
She delved deeper.

rules.name: "It's not X, it's Y"
rules.message: The "it's not X, it's Y" setup reads as AI.
rules.why: Setting up a contrast just to knock it down is one of the most common AI sentence shapes. Readers spot it quickly.
rules.fix: Say the point directly: keep the Y part and drop the X part.

flag: It's not a tool, it's a movement.
This is not just about money; it's about trust.
pass: It's not ready yet, so we wait.

rules.name: "In today's fast-paced world"
rules.why: Generic scene-setting openers are a classic sign of filler writing, and AI models reach for them constantly.
rules.fix: Start with your actual point or a specific fact.

flag: In today's fast-paced world, time is money.
In today’s digital landscape, brands must adapt.
pass: Today the store opens at nine.

rules.name: "Tapestry"
rules.message: "Tapestry" used as a metaphor reads as AI.
rules.why: Describing things as a "rich tapestry" is a favorite AI metaphor and rarely adds meaning.
rules.fix: Name the actual things you mean.

flag: The city is a rich tapestry of cultures.
pass: The museum restored a medieval rug.

rules.name: "A testament to"
rules.why: This phrase shows up constantly in AI writing to add weight without adding facts.
rules.fix: Say what the thing proves, with a specific detail.

flag: The award is a testament to our team's hard work.
pass: The team won the award after two years of work.

rules.name: "Navigate the landscape"
rules.why: Abstract travel metaphors like this are common in AI text and vague for readers.
rules.fix: Say what the person actually has to do.

flag: We help you navigate the complex landscape of taxes.
pass: We help you file your taxes on time.

rules.name: Hype words
rules.message: This hype phrase reads as AI.
rules.why: Big claims with no evidence are common in AI marketing copy. Readers skim past them.
rules.fix: Replace the claim with a number or a concrete result.

flag: This app is a game-changer for teams.
Unlock the full potential of your data.
pass: This app cut our meeting time in half.

rules.name: "Let's dive in"
rules.why: Announcing that you are about to start is filler, and AI models open with it all the time.
rules.fix: Delete it and start with the first real point.

flag: Let's dive into the details.
We'll jump right in.

rules.name: Closing filler
rules.message: This stock phrase reads as AI.
rules.why: Stock openers and sign-offs are the first thing readers notice in AI emails and posts.
rules.fix: End with the next step or simply stop when you are done.

flag: I hope this helps!
In conclusion, the plan works.

rules.name: Reveal setups
rules.message: This reveal setup reads as AI.
rules.why: Teasing a point before making it ("Here's the thing") is a common AI hook, especially on social media.
rules.fix: Make the point without the drumroll.

flag: Here's the thing: nobody reads the manual.
The kicker? It was free.

rules.name: Corporate buzzwords
rules.why: These words are everywhere in AI business writing and say very little on their own.
rules.fix: Use a plain verb and say exactly what changes.

flag: Seamlessly integrate your tools.
Leverage our platform to grow.
pass: Connect your tools in two clicks.

rules.name: Stiff transition openers
rules.message: Opening with "Moreover" or "Furthermore" reads as AI.
rules.why: Formal transition words at the start of sentences are much more common in AI text than in natural writing.
rules.fix: Drop the transition, or use "Also" or "And".

flag: It is fast. Moreover, it is cheap.
Furthermore, the team agreed.
pass: It is fast and it is cheap.

rules.name: "It's worth noting"
rules.message: "It's worth noting that" reads as AI.
rules.why: This phrase adds words before the point without adding meaning. AI models use it constantly.
rules.fix: Delete the phrase and state the fact.

flag: It's worth noting that prices rose.

rules.name: "Plays a crucial role"
rules.message: "Plays a crucial role" reads as AI.
rules.why: This is one of the most frequent AI phrases. It sounds important but hides what actually happens.
rules.fix: Say what the thing does, specifically.

flag: Sleep plays a crucial role in health.
pass: Sleep repairs muscle and fixes memories.
